article.title: How to Find a Stud Without a Stud Finder
article.summary: Find wall studs with no stud finder: use outlets, trim nails, measuring and a magnet, then confirm with a hidden test nail before you hang anything.
article.body:
You can find studs reliably with what's in a junk drawer, because houses are framed on a predictable pattern. Use two or three of these clues together, then always confirm with a small test hole that your shelf or mount will cover.

Affiliate disclosure: some links in this guide are affiliate links. If you buy through them, we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. We only recommend products we'd use ourselves.

Safety: wires and pipes often run along studs and up from outlets and switches. Don't drive test nails directly above or below an outlet or switch.

Steps

  1. Start at an outlet or switch

    Electrical boxes are usually nailed to one side of a stud. Remove the cover plate (outlets are safe to touch with the plate off, but keep fingers out of the box) and look or tap to see which side of the box is fastened.

    Done right: you know which side of the box the stud is on. Mark about 3/4 in past that edge on the wall.

  2. Measure on 16 in centers

    From your first stud, measure along the wall in 16 in steps: most U.S. walls have studs 16 in apart, center to center (some are 24 in). Mark each spot lightly on painter's tape.

    Done right: you have a row of likely stud marks across the wall.

  3. Find the fasteners with a magnet

    Slide a strong magnet slowly up and down near your marks. It sticks where drywall screws or nails go into the stud. You'll find a vertical line of them on each stud.

    Done right: the magnet sticks at two or more spots in a vertical line.

  4. Read the trim and the light

    Baseboard and crown nails usually go into studs, so look for filled nail holes in the trim. Then shine a flashlight flat across the wall: screw dimples often show as faint dots in a vertical line.

    Done right: the trim nails and dimples line up with your 16 in marks.

  5. Confirm with a hidden test nail

    Where your shelf or bracket will cover the hole, tap in a thin finish nail. Over a stud, it stops hard after about 1/2 in. If it slides through easily, you're between studs: try 3/4 in to either side.

    Done right: the nail hits solid wood, and you've marked the stud's center.

Get help if: the wall is plaster and lath (studs are harder to find and walls crack easily), you're mounting a TV or anything very heavy, or the wall is masonry.

FAQ

How far apart are studs?

Usually 16 in from center to center in U.S. homes, sometimes 24 in, especially in newer homes and garages.

Does knocking on the wall work?

It helps a bit: the wall sounds duller and more solid over a stud. It's unreliable on its own, so combine it with other clues.

Is there an app that finds studs?

Phone magnetometer apps can find screws, much like a magnet does. They don't see the wood itself.

How wide is a stud?

Standard 2×4 studs are 1-1/2 in wide, so aim for the center to give screws the most wood.
